stories.headline: Attack on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery kills a worker
body: A projectile hit an oil refinery in Jazan on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast, killing a Nepali worker and injuring several people.
It caused a fire and briefly halted some operations.
The Saudi-led coalition blamed Yemen's Houthis.
stories.vc: Attacks on Saudi oil sites add risk to global fuel prices.

stories.headline: Mexico wants US talks over suspected SpaceX debris
body: Mexico is seeking talks with US aviation authorities about rocket debris from SpaceX launches in Texas.
President Claudia Sheinbaum said Mexico may ask for limits on airspace use or even moving the launch site.
Mexican authorities recovered debris after a Starship launch this month.
stories.joke: Space junk, now an international postal problem.
stories.vc: Launch limits could slow SpaceX's busy Starship schedule.

stories.headline: Italy rebukes Ukraine for striking Russian ships off Libya
body: Italy said Ukraine was wrong to 'violate Libya's sovereignty' by attacking Russian vessels there.
It is a rare crack in Rome's support for Kyiv.
Analysts say Italy fears instability in Libya could hurt its energy interests and migration controls.
stories.vc: Libyan instability threatens Italy's gas supplies.

stories.headline: Markets rise for a second day as IT stocks lead
body: The Sensex rose 390 points to 84,328.59 and the Nifty closed at 25,884.50.
HCL Tech jumped 6.28%, leading IT stocks higher.
Foreign fund buying continued to lift sentiment.
stories.vc: Steady foreign inflows support the rupee and Indian shares.

stories.statLabel: Tata Trusts' stake in Tata Sons
stories.headline: Tata Trusts goes to court against Chandrasekaran's reappointment
body: Tata Trusts, which owns 66% of Tata Sons, filed two suits in the Bombay High Court.
It challenges N. Chandrasekaran's reappointment as executive chairman for a third term.
The hearing is set for Friday.
stories.vc: A boardroom fight could unsettle investors in Tata group companies.

stories.headline: Yes Bank AT1 verdict could leave 60 lakh shareholders footing the bill
body: The Supreme Court upheld an order quashing the 2020 write-down of Yes Bank's AT1 bonds.
It said the rescue administrator lacked authority to write them down.
Analysts warn about 60 lakh small shareholders may share the ₹8,415 crore cost.
stories.joke: Bondholders win; shareholders get the bill.
stories.vc: The case sets a precedent for how bank rescues treat risky bonds.

stories.headline: Unhedged: what should a fund manager do in choppy markets?
body: FT's Unhedged podcast says stocks, bonds and even gold are swinging wildly.
Gold, usually a safe haven, touched its lowest level in a year.
Katie Martin asks ex-fund manager Toby Nangle how to navigate it.
stories.joke: Even the safe haven needs a safe haven.
stories.vc: When everything moves together, spreading risk gets harder.

stories.statLabel: China AI compute via remote data centres
stories.headline: Nvidia pauses server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
body: Nvidia told partners like Dell and Super Micro to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the WSJ reports.
Chinese firms had used data centres there to access Nvidia chips remotely.
A think tank estimates such sites supply about 24% of China's AI compute. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.vc: Tighter controls could slow Nvidia's sales growth in Asia.

stories.headline: Musk says every US child will get two SpaceX shares
body: SpaceX will give one new share to every active 'Trump Account', and Musk says he'll personally match it.
That means two shares per child, Musk posted on X.
SpaceX didn't say whether any conditions apply. (No new Stratechery post, so this is a Reuters report via The Hindu.)
stories.vc: Gifting shares makes millions of children SpaceX shareholders.

stories.headline: GEF Capital raises $615M for its biggest India climate fund
body: GEF Capital Partners closed $615 million for its fourth India climate fund.
It is 40% larger than its previous $440 million fund.
Its portfolio includes ReNew Power, Indian Energy Exchange and Yulu. (TechCrunch Venture had no fresh deal, so this is Inc42's report.)
stories.vc: Big climate funds signal investor confidence in India's energy shift.

stories.headline: Norse Atlantic suspends flights and warns of bankruptcy
body: Budget long-haul airline Norse Atlantic suspended all flights on Thursday.
Its board says it will file for bankruptcy unless urgent short-term financing is found.
Its shares fell 85% after it called its finances 'critical'. (No Economist piece was readable, so this is a Reuters report via The Hindu.)
stories.vc: Budget long-haul flying remains a tough business.

stories.headline: A Rajasthan schoolgirl secretly stopped her own child marriage
body: A 16-year-old in Sikar called the 1098 child helpline over six times after her family fixed her wedding.
Officials got a court order and stopped it with 72 hours to spare.
Sikar prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025.
stories.vc: Girls who stay in school are more likely to earn and be independent.

stories.headline: Thousands march in Madrid to defend Spain's gender-violence law
body: Thousands marched in Madrid to defend Spain's protections against violence on women before Sunday's election.
Far-right Vox wants to repeal the landmark 2004 law.
Polls suggest the conservative PP may need Vox to govern.
stories.vc: Protections for women affect their safety at home and at work.

stories.headline: Protesters across the Balkans demand action on violence against women
body: People marched in Bulgaria, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Turkey on November 25.
In Sofia, they called for better data, more shelters and prevention plans.
In Kosovo, organisers want femicide made a separate crime.
stories.vc: Shelters and prevention need steady public funding.

stories.headline: Guwahati's GMCH gets an 870-bed annex hospital on December 2
body: Assam's CM Himanta Biswa Sarma will open an 870-bed hospital attached to Gauhati Medical College on December 2.
It has about 120 ICU beds with ventilators.
Seven departments, including emergency and surgery, will move in.
stories.vc: A big boost in ICU beds strengthens emergency care across the Northeast.

stories.headline: UP hands four government hospitals to private operators
body: Uttar Pradesh approved private operators to run four government hospital facilities for 30 years.
They include a 300-bed hospital in Bareilly and a 200-bed hospital in Banda.
Health group Jan Swasthya Abhiyan has criticised the move.
stories.vc: PPP deals can add investment but raise concerns about costs for poor patients.

stories.headline: Fortis Noida opens a lung failure clinic
body: Fortis Hospital Noida launched a clinic for advanced and end-stage lung disease.
It will spot patients early who may need a lung transplant.
It covers conditions like pulmonary fibrosis and COPD.
stories.vc: Specialist clinics help hospital chains grow high-value services.

stories.headline: Moscow Exchange's derivatives revenue jumps 52%
body: Derivatives brought MOEX RUB 4.63 billion ($56.2 million) in fees in Q3, up nearly 53%.
Trading volume rose 62.4% to RUB 55.16 trillion.
Currency derivatives turnover jumped 81%.
stories.vc: Fee income grew slower than volume as cheaper contracts dominated.

stories.statLabel: T+1 start in EU, UK, Switzerland
stories.headline: Pirum launches a tool to match settlement details before T+1
body: Pirum launched SSIConnect, which matches standing settlement instructions across a trade's life.
It prepares firms for T+1 settlement in the EU, UK and Switzerland on 11 October 2027.
It can plug into firms' existing systems.
stories.vc: Shorter settlement leaves less time to fix errors.

stories.headline: Explainer: What does 'T+1 settlement' mean?
body: Imagine you agree to swap cricket cards at school today, but the actual cards change hands tomorrow.
Grown-ups call that handover 'settlement'. 'T+1' means it happens one day after the trade.
The EU, UK and Switzerland move to T+1 on 11 October 2027.
This week, Pirum launched a tool so firms can match payment details in time.
A shorter wait means less time for things to go wrong between the deal and the delivery.
stories.vc: Speedier settlement cuts risk.

stories.headline: Haas finally confirms Oliver Bearman for 2027
body: Haas has signed Oliver Bearman for 2027, alongside Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara.
That completes the 2027 grid before the last two races of 2026.
Bearman has scored 23 of Haas' 31 points this season.
stories.vc: Keeping its star driver helps Haas pitch to sponsors.
